title: I built a PS1-style horror game set on an abandoned oil rig
author: BearDazzling7282
selftext:
It's called Albatros-7, a short first person horror game on an oil rig in the middle of a storm. You are on a night watch, it's 3:12 AM and a boat shows up that nobody else heard. Free, runs in the browser, also on mobile: [https://albatros7.glworx.com](https://albatros7.glworx.com)



I made it with Claude Code (Opus 5.5), talking to it in Spanish. Mostly I'd play it, tell it what felt off, and it would go fix it. It's plain three.js, no engine. The whole rig and all the textures are generated in code, there's no image file for the level at all. The PS1 look is a custom shader (vertex snapping, dithering, fog, a flashlight cone), and the security camera that shows you asleep in your own bed is an actual second camera rendering to the monitor.



Not everything is AI though. The characters are from Elbolilloduro's free Characters PSX pack, because the people Opus made itself were honestly pretty bad, stiff blocky dolls. That was the most frustrating part. Once I had the pack it loaded the rigged models and posed them with the skeletons, and later wrote a simple walk and climb cycle so they'd stop floating around. Music and sounds are CC0 stuff from freesound that Claude Code picked.



The part that surprised me the most was the trailer creation. I just asked for one and it did the whole thing: it took over the game's clock so it could step it frame by frame at 30fps and save every frame, scripted the camera shots and the scares, then cut it all with ffmpeg, with the text in the game's own pixel font and the music and sound effects mixed in. It even checked its own work by making contact sheets of the frames, and fixed stuff like a figure walking out of shot or the glass cracks looking like a spiderweb.



Please let me know what you think about it, and I hope it's not another AI slop.
